    base,
    quote,
    rate,
    _loaded_at,
    _sim_loaded_at,

from "warehouse"."raw"."fx_rates"

-- Daily files are full snapshots: keep only the latest one.
select
    customer_id,
    email,
    full_name,
    country,
    nullif(signup_date, '')::date as signup_date,
    segment,
    business_date,
    _loaded_at,
    _sim_loaded_at,
    _source_file,
    _batch_id
from "warehouse"."raw"."customers"
where business_date = (select max(business_date) from "warehouse"."raw"."customers")

-- Spine from day0 to the current sim date. The bounds are read from the sim clock at run time, so a
-- generate_series is used rather than dbt_utils.date_spine (which needs compile-time literals).
select
    d::date as date_day,
    extract(year from d)::int as year,
    extract(month from d)::int as month,
    extract(day from d)::int as day_of_month,
    extract(isodow from d)::int as iso_day_of_week,
    to_char(d, 'Dy') as day_name,
    extract(isodow from d) in (6, 7) as is_weekend
from generate_series(
    (select day0 from control.sim_clock where id = 1),
    (control.sim_now() at time zone 'UTC')::date,
    interval '1 day'
) as d

-- Daily files are full snapshots: keep only the latest one.

    _loaded_at,
    _sim_loaded_at,
    _source_file,
    _batch_id
from "warehouse"."raw"."products"
where business_date = (select max(business_date) from "warehouse"."raw"."products")

-- As arrived, typed. No trimming, cleaning or deduplication. Blank strings become NULL so that a bad
-- value surfaces as a failing not_null test instead of a cast error.

    (nullif(quantity, '')::int * nullif(unit_price, '')::numeric(12, 2))::numeric(12, 2) as line_amount,

-- One row per order_line_id; the latest _loaded_at wins. duplicate_count = extra raw copies of this line
-- (sum it by business_date for the per-day duplicate volume).
with ranked as (
    select
        *,
        row_number() over (partition by order_line_id order by _loaded_at desc) as rn,
        count(*) over (partition by order_line_id) - 1 as duplicate_count
    from "warehouse"."staging"."stg_sales"
)

select
    order_id,
    order_line_id,
    order_date,
    order_ts,
    customer_id,
    product_id,
    quantity,
    unit_price,
    line_amount,
    currency,
    line_type,
    channel,
    business_date,
    _loaded_at,
    duplicate_count
from ranked
where rn = 1

-- As-of FX join: each line takes the latest rate on or before its order_date (weekends and holidays fall back
-- to the previous business day). GBP needs no rate. revenue_gbp stays NULL when no rate exists, which the
-- not_null test on fct_sales catches.
select
    s.order_id,
    s.order_line_id,
    s.order_date,
    s.order_ts,
    s.customer_id,
    s.product_id,
    s.quantity,
    s.unit_price,
    s.line_amount,
    s.currency,
    s.line_type,
    s.channel,
    s.business_date,
    s.duplicate_count,
    case when s.currency = 'GBP' then 1::numeric else fx.rate end as fx_rate,
    case
        when s.currency = 'GBP' then s.line_amount
        else round(s.line_amount / fx.rate, 2)
    end as revenue_gbp
from "warehouse"."intermediate"."int_sales_deduped" as s
left join lateral (
    select f.rate
    from "warehouse"."staging"."stg_fx_rates" as f
    where f.base = 'GBP'
      and f.quote = s.currency
      and f.rate_date <= s.order_date
    order by f.rate_date desc
    limit 1
) as fx on true

select

    line_type,
    quantity,
    unit_price,
    line_amount,
    revenue_gbp
from "warehouse"."intermediate"."int_orders_enriched"
